questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that it were the only option outside of Europe and was a destination I wouldn't easily be able to visit otherwise.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy as long as you read all the emails from the university - and there were a lot of those!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: From the moment we sent our application and till the end we received information from a study abroad advisor from the host university, so most information were given to us before we even arrived in Australia. Before the start of the semester there were also a mandatory introduction for exchange and study abroad student with additional information and it was also an opportunity to ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The off campus housing I stayed in were still student accommodation and it was one of the options provided by the host university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of how long transport to university takes. Sydney is a large city so you can quickly have quite some transportation time for uni.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was okay, there were some things that were a little unclear but I had the advantage of knowing someone who had been there the year before and also knowing others who were going at the same time as I was, so we helped each other out with questions and figured it out between us.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as being fairly straight forward as long as you had the required documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had the option of emailing a study abroad advisor from the host university, however, she took her sweet time responding.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was one class I couldn't get because the host university cancelled it for the semester which was too bad. We couldn't get approval for that many courses from our faculty in Copenhagen so of the classes I could get approved, I got the classes I wanted (which weren't cancelled).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get it done as soon as the email about it arrives so you have time to ask questions and wait for answers.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did my bachelors thesis there which was really nice in terms of the level, at the beginning there were some confusion but this was solved during the semester. For my two courses, I had PCOL3012 (drug design and development) which was fairly straightforward with my knowledge from courses in Denmark. Then I had HPSC1000 (bioethics). Both courses had a fairly light workload compared to what I'm used to at UCPH but that was nice as it gave me time to focus on my thesis and explore. The courses were easier than what I'm used to in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was kind of similar, there are lectures (which are videotaped!), then there is lab work in some of the courses and then there is tutorials which are more class work or class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PCOL3012 - drug design and development
HPSC1000 - bioethics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend both PCOL3012 and HPSC1000. PCOL3012 matches up nicely with what has been reached already at pharmacy at UCPH and the workload is not too bad. HPSC1000 is a pretty chill course as well.
Both courses don't have that many compulsory classes, I managed to only have compulsory classes on Wednesday which gave me a lot of freedom for exploring and doing my bachelors thesis.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent is expensive here but everything else is not too bad.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different clubs with different cultural backgrounds, different sports clubs and stuff like that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the opportunities through USU, such as campus tours and day trips. Campus tours are great for getting to know campus and the day trips are free trips to someplace in Sydney where you have the opportunity to explore and make friends from the beginning.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Blue Mountains is really great, don't do just a day trip, book somewhere to sleep up there so you have the opportunity to explore more.
New Zealand in mid-semester break is a great opportunity.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for Mates Abroad to get to know a local student who has been on exchange and also get to know other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that they don't really bike.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It's more laid back than in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Meet as many new people as possible - they are the ones who are going to make your stay amazing.
Consider what you want to prioritise when you are finding accommodation - do you want to be close to uni or close to the beach? Both aren't really an option.
Explore the city and surroundings and the country as much as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you can, set notifications for the emails from the study abroad advisor - the one about housing comes in the middle of the night and if you want the cheapest housing on campus you have to be quick, otherwise it will be full and you have to take some of the other options.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many different people and exploring a new country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Arrive prior to the start of the semester - the jetlag can be a bitch.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
